subject: Pilot economics: budget anchors, cache/batch levers, and next-step asks
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@fincent.com>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@fincent.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot economics: budget anchors, cache/batch levers, and next-step asks

Thanks for taking the time today — quick follow-up to lock down the things we agreed on and the next steps so nothing falls through the cracks. I’ve summarized the call below and attached a first-pass pilot cost workbook + M.A.P. for reference.

Short summary / pain points you highlighted:
- Token spend visibility: billing today is coarse; team needs per-route token breakdown for conversational flows.
- Peak/latency sensitivity: spikes during reconciliation windows cause timeouts; target p95 < 150ms for the high-priority endpoint.
- Budget constraint: initial cap ~ $45k/month for pilot scope unless we shift to committed capacity.
- Ops constraints: security/compliance will require customer-managed keys and audit logs for the pilot.

Desired outcomes (what success looks like in 8 weeks):
- 60% reduction in per-transaction inference cost vs your current hosted baseline (measured on sample workload).
- Stable p95 latency under 150ms for the primary flow.
- Clear runbook + M.A.P. with rollout milestones and rollback criteria.

Levers we discussed (cost/TCO focused):
1) Prefix/KV caching for repeated context slices — expect 20–40% token reduction on the high-frequency reconciliation messages.
2) Micro-batching (50–200ms tradeoff window) for non-interactive back-office workloads to improve GPU utilization.
3) Model tiering + quantized variants: use a smaller quantized model for intent classification and NER; reserve the larger model only for generative responses.
4) Reserved vs on-demand: committed Dedicated capacity reduces per-token compute by ~30% but requires a 3-month minimum commitment for the pricing shown in the workbook.

Immediate next steps (I’ll own items 1–3):
- I’ll drop the redwood-pilot-cost-model.xlsx (attached) with two pricing scenarios: hosted API and Dedicated-reserved (Marissa will help finalize commercial terms).
- Marissa: can you prepare two commercial scenarios (monthly hosted vs 3-month reserved) and a short note on minimum commitment flex?
- FinCent: confirm the pilot scope we should model (approx monthly calls, avg tokens per call, peak QPS windows) — Priya if you can share the QA sample trace that would be ideal.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-cost-model.xlsx (first-pass), mutual-action-plan.docx (M.A.P. template)

Thanks again — we’ll aim to have the cost scenarios and a recommended pilot config by COB Thu (10/8).

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: redwood-pilot-cost-model.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)]
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan.docx (docx, 16KB)]

From: Daniel Cho <daniel@fincent.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@fincent.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics: budget anchors, cache/batch levers, and next-step asks

Thanks — good write-up, Evelyn. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- Budget: $45k/month is the target for the pilot but we could stretch to $60k/month if the reserved capacity case clearly shows a positive ROI within the quarter.
- Compliance: we will need KMS integration and event-level audit logs — security can sign a narrow scope for pilot if those are present.
- Scope to model: assume 250k user interactions / month, avg 420 tokens per interaction, with peak QPS ~ 45 during daily reconciliation windows.

Priya and I will drop the QA trace by EOD tomorrow. Also — can Redwood show an example of the cache-hit distribution you’ve seen on a similar customer? That will help us gauge whether 20–40% token reduction is realistic.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: FinCent pilot — commercial scenarios and quick-win asks

Marissa/Ben — quick internal note based on FinCent call: they gave us explicit numbers (250k interactions/mo, ~420 tokens/interaction, peak 45 QPS). The customer is budget-constrained (~$45k/mo preferred, $60k/mo stretch) and needs KMS + audit logs.

Please prioritize two outputs by Thu COB: 
1) Marissa: two-sided pricing (hosted, and 3-month reserved/dedicated) with clear per-token and per-peak-QPS math + proposed commitment flex. Highlight what discount levels map to $45k vs $60k.
2) Ben: can you run a quick conservative hit-rate model for prefix/KV caching using the sample trace they’ll share? I want a baseline projection (10/20/30/40% hit-rate scenarios) and an expected per-transaction token reduction.

Notes for messaging to FinCent: emphasize quick wins they can enable without infra changes (prompt canonicalization + route-level caching) and then the second wave (reserved capacity + model tiering) for deeper savings.

Looping Marissa and Ben now. I’ll circulate the first-pass workbook and the M.A.P. before EOD Thu.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Fri (10/9): Ben provides caching hit-rate sensitivity table after he gets the QA trace.
- Mon (10/12): commercial review call (15–30m) to agree on pilot commitment and any required security scoping.

Two asks for you:

2) Daniel — confirm whether security needs us to use your customer KMS for the pilot or a scoped alternative (we can support both).

Evelyn
